title: What can you say about choline in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for choline; the strongest is "Supports normal liver function" (strong, 27-1,000 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats fatty liver disease (NAFLD)".

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists liver function, and the EU authorizes maintenance of normal liver function after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 27-1,000 mg a day for ages 14 and older (19-1,000 mg for children 1 to 13), counted as choline itself, not the weight of the salt. EU: the food must contain at least 82.5 mg of choline per 100 g, 100 ml or single portion. 3,500 mg a day is the ODS upper limit for adults.
supported_wordings.form: Choline from choline bitartrate, chloride, citrate or another listed salt, counted as choline

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease; the supported wording is normal liver function.
Implies removing damage or toxins from an organ; the supported wording is normal liver function.
Names diseases; no listed source supports brain or memory wording for choline.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
